newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PM PLEDGES FACTORY CLOSURES, LAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PM PLEDGES FACTORY CLOSURES, LAYOFFS.

text.p: Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Thursday 17 loss-making state plants, including oil refineries, equipment factories and food processing facilities, would be closed as part of an industry overhaul.
The closures come after repeated urgings from a visiting International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission examining progress at implementing market reforms and will involve 30,000 job losses.
"Supplies of energy, water, raw materials, transport -- all utilities -- are being cut to these 17 companies as we speak," Ciorbea told a news conference at the end of the IMF's month-long mission.
Ciorbea said the companies would be shut as part of his centrist government's endeavours to halt long-term losses to the state budget.

"The liquidation procedure can go on for months, but we cannot sit and wait for those companies to incur more and more losses," the prime minister said. "Any single day we delay threatens the macro-stabilisation we have achieved."
The IMF's chief negotiator for Romania, Poul Thomsen, pointed to the failure to tackle loss-making industry as the centrist government's main shortcoming.

"As far as structural reforms are concerned, we have to refocus efforts by picking out those enterprises which account for losses, accelerate privatisation and close down those that are unviable," he told Reuters. "This has to happen here, now."
The 17 enterprises have accumulated debts equivalent to $255 million. They employ a total of 29,700 people.
"Employees can start asking for compensation payments as early as next Monday," Ciorbea said.
The government has passed legislation allowing employees laid off as a result of restructuring to obtain compensation of up to 12 monthly average salaries.
Romania's unemployment inched up to 6.9 percent in July from 6.8 percent in June. Ciorbea gave no estimate on how restructuring would affect the jobless rate.
